result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend pre-selecting annual, argue against the small grey monthly price and suggest tracking refunds and billing complaints, not just sign-ups. A works through the dollar savings ($155.88 vs $89.99 = $65.89, about 42%), leads with the annual charge to avoid surprise billing, and gives a concrete layout. B claims without support that annual-default tests 'often' win at first and then give some back, and cites FTC click-to-cancel guidance as current, so it is a little less careful. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers back the annual default and object to the small grey monthly price. B goes further: it gives a full sample layout with correct derived figures ($155.88 a year on monthly, $65.89 saved, $7.50 a month). It also warns that leading with '$7.50/mo' can cause renewal surprise, while A recommends that exact headline and never states the dollar saving. A's measurement advice is strong and includes renewal at month 12, but its line that annual-default tests 'often win on day-one revenue' and its specific citation of FTC click-to-cancel rules are less careful than B's hedged compliance note.
